Conformist

/kuhn-FOR-mist/ - the stress falls on FOR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Conformist means a person who behaves the same way as everyone around them.

A conformist to the last, Deng studied the other diners before ordering exactly what the next table had.

Worked Example

Every station in the market row sells the same three phone cases now. Rivera stocked hand-lettered ones for a month, watched two neighboring vendors smirk, and quietly went back to the bestseller list everyone else orders from. Nothing forced the change — no fine, no rule. The stalls on either side simply never varied, and in the end neither did he.

Conformist is the exact word for Rivera, because a conformist is a person who behaves the same way as everyone around them — the pull is the crowd itself, not any official rule. Follower is looser: a follower trails a leader or a trend and may still keep private tastes; the conformist's tastes surrender too.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

follower: goes along with a leader or a trend, but may keep private opinions

copycat: imitates a particular person; the conformist matches the whole crowd

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

individualist: sets their own course and wears the difference openly

rebel: pushes against the crowd on purpose

Where it sits · how fully independent choice is surrendered — follower → conformist → sheep

follower vs. conformist: A follower falls in behind a leader or a fashion, and may still keep a private opinion or two.

sheep vs. conformist: Sheep goes further than conformist — the conformist still chooses to match the crowd, while calling people sheep says the choosing has stopped altogether.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: with, together

Root — form

Root — form: shape (Latin forma)

Suffix — -ist

Suffix — -ist: a person who

Put it together

Put it together: Con- (together) + form (shape) + -ist (person) = a person shaped together with everyone else. The word is its own picture: take the crowd's form, press yourself into it, and sign your name with -ist.

Use the root in a new word: formation

Use the root in a new word: formation: Geese fly in formation — a single shape the whole flock holds together, every bird keeping the form.

Root Check

Word Choice

mildly critical

Conformist carries a raised eyebrow: it names someone whose choices dissolve into the crowd's. Keep it apart from its unit-mates — compliant means meeting written rules, and obedience answers a person in authority; the conformist obeys nobody in particular, only the pressure of everybody. A traditionalist, on the other hand, holds to the past even when the crowd moves on.
